# montecarlo_sql_server_credentials (Resource)

SQL Server credentials are the login Monte Carlo stores for SQL Server connections to use: a SQL login, or Windows Authentication with Kerberos. The password and the keytab are never returned.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A SQL Server connection with credentials Monte Carlo stores: the warehouse, a
# database user and its password, and the connection that joins them.
#
# The warehouse type is taken from `connection_type`: SQL Server connections
# live on a `transactional-db` warehouse.
#
# To keep the password in your own store instead, use one of the self-hosted
# credentials resources.
#
# See https://docs.getmontecarlo.com/docs/sql-server for creating the user and
# granting it the reads Monte Carlo needs.

terraform {
  # Write-only arguments need Terraform 1.11 or later.
  required_version = ">= 1.11"

  required_providers {
    montecarlo = {
      source = "monte-carlo-data/montecarlo"
    }
  }
}

provider "montecarlo" {
  # Credentials come from the environment or from the Monte Carlo CLI's profile.
  # See the provider documentation for the alternatives.
}

# The `montecarlo_warehouse` example shows the deployment and agent behind
# `deployment_id`.
resource "montecarlo_warehouse" "sql_server" {
  name            = "production-sql-server"
  connection_type = "sql-server"
  deployment_id   = "<deployment id, from the Monte Carlo app>"
}

resource "montecarlo_sql_server_credentials" "sql_server" {
  host    = "sqlserver.example.com"
  port    = 1433
  db_name = "analytics"

  # A SQL login. For Kerberos, set `auth_mode = "kerberos"` with `realm`, `kdc`,
  # `principal` and a keytab or password instead of `user`.
  auth_mode = "sql"
  user      = "monte_carlo"

  # In a real configuration, pass the password from a sensitive variable or a
  # secret store rather than a literal in a committed file.
  #
  # Write-only, so never stored in state or a plan. Changing it alone plans
  # nothing: bump the version with it.
  password_wo         = "..."
  password_wo_version = 1
}

# The connection's type comes from the credentials, and has to fit the
# warehouse's type.
resource "montecarlo_connection" "sql_server" {
  name           = "production-sql-server"
  warehouse_id   = montecarlo_warehouse.sql_server.id
  credentials_id = montecarlo_sql_server_credentials.sql_server.id
}

output "connection_id" {
  description = "Id of the connection."
  value       = montecarlo_connection.sql_server.id
}

output "connection_type" {
  description = "What the connection reaches, taken from the credentials."
  value       = montecarlo_connection.sql_server.connection_type
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host` (String) Hostname of the database endpoint. For `kerberos`, the fully qualified name the server's service principal is registered under.
- `port` (Number) Port the database listens on.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth_mode` (String) How Monte Carlo signs in. `sql` takes `user` and `password`. `kerberos` takes `realm`, `kdc`, `principal`, and one of `keytab_base64` or `password`.
- `db_name` (String) Database to connect to.
- `kdc` (String) Hostname of the key distribution center, optionally with `:port`, for `kerberos`.
- `keytab_base64_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Base64-encoded keytab for `principal`, for `kerberos`. Send this or `password`. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `keytab_base64_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `keytab_base64_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of `user` for `sql`, or of the Active Directory account behind `principal` for `kerberos`. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `password_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `principal` (String) Active Directory principal Monte Carlo signs in as, for `kerberos`.
- `realm` (String) Kerberos realm, normally the Active Directory domain in capitals, for `kerberos`.
- `user` (String) SQL login Monte Carlo signs in as, for `sql`.

### Read-Only

- `connection_type` (String) The connection type the credentials are for, such as `snowflake`. Fixed once created.
- `created_time` (String) When the credentials were created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the credentials.
- `storage_type` (String) Where the secret lives. Fixed once created.
